correctness.rationale: For a two-row ladder every connected vertex subset occupies a column interval; domination forces endpoints at first/second and last/penultimate columns. If an endpoint column is occupied it must begin TT or DD, whereas an omitted endpoint needs adjacent B; analogous right rules. Interior double columns B are indispensable only if neighboring singleton runs lie in opposite rows, so all internal B occur in TBD or DBT, and unseparated singleton columns share a row. Conversely those words dominate, connect, and every deletion destroys domination or connectivity. Connected domination is upward closed, making single-deletion tests equivalent to inclusion-minimality. Decomposing disjoint singleton runs and switching B columns yields bivariate GF 2V+(2BV^2+4xBV+2x^2B^2U)/(1-BU)+x^2B+x^2B^2+2x^2y^2, U=xy/(1-xy), V=x^2y^2/(1-xy), B=xy^2. y=1 gives (4x^2-x^3-x^6)/(1-x-x^2), so a2=4,a3=3,a4=7 and a_n=2F_n for n>=5. Independent vertex-subset enumeration n=2..8 exactly verified counts 4,3,7,10,16,26,42 and corresponding size profiles; this does not replace all-n proof.
